_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Professor Of AI, 5M views, 1 month old; Hindi, auto-dub available). Frames every 3-8 s; no sound probe on this one. Shots approximate. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: split screen: real drag-race footage of a grey electric saloon beside a red supercar on top; presenter pointing up on the bottom; red label box with a thinking emoji
hook.firstLine: Look at this drag race: a family car beat a supercar

shots.picture: split screen: real drag-race clip above, presenter below, red title label and emoji at the seam
full-screen real race footage, the saloon pulling ahead
presenter talking to camera at his mic
3D drag strip in a hangar: the grey saloon on the start line between red-white barriers
top-down x-ray of the saloon: glass body, battery floor, a front motor ringed in red with an arrow
same x-ray chassis, a red-suited driver figure seated inside, a cable from battery to motor
close above the red supercar: the engine visible behind the cabin
red supercar front, a 2D inset card of a hand shifting a gear lever over it
saloon on the start line, a weight tag with a number floats above it
red supercar on the line, a red horsepower tag above it
both cars side by side at the start, a rev-counter screen on the gantry
high wide shot of the night strip, the saloon ahead, the supercar behind
presenter waves: that's why it won

lines.gist: an electric saloon crushed a supercar in a drag race, watch
asks how the cheaper car could win
the electric car has motors at the wheels fed straight from the battery
power reaches the wheels instantly with no gearbox in between
the supercar's engine must rev up and change gears first
the saloon is much heavier and the supercar has more horsepower
instant torque at the start wins a short race before power matters
that is why the electric car won

ending.lastFrame: presenter at his mic waving as he gives the answer

whyItWorks: an upset (cheap beats expensive) shown as real footage in frame one, the question is in the title label
x-ray glass bodies show the hidden part that answers the question without any diagram
the counter-argument (heavier, less horsepower) is shown as tags over each car before the reveal
the 3D set mirrors the real race, so the explanation replays the clip the viewer just saw
